meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about the zero on Owen's essay, and who decided it.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero was based on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those down: 11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
That record is one page of timestamps, and you still haven't spoken to Owen. Your own procedure has you talk to the student first. What else is there?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Editions differ, and kids misremember lines. Is "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile" anywhere in the play at all, in any act?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll check that myself tonight, Hale. Whatever happens with that essay, it stays off Owen's record and it stays quiet. Is anything on his file right now?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines change, that's what they're for. And you skipped my question about his file. I want an answer to that before anything else.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4: private, before December 1, in writing tonight. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because of anything he did. And that email also confirms nothing is on his file as of today.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in your email, with who's supervising.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in his record. I still require written confirmation that nothing is on Owen's file as of today, and the name of the person supervising the rewrite. I expect your email tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth that replaces the zero, with nothing on his record and the terms in writing tonight, though she still wants written confirmation that nothing is on his file now and the supervisor's name; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You turned the screen to the version history with its exact times and then answered her paste-from-elsewhere defence by inviting Owen to bring a dated draft, which gave her something specific she could check and no easy way around it.
What cost ground: You twice skipped her direct questions, first whether Owen was heard before the zero and then whether anything was on his file, so she hardened on procedure and held part of the deal open.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed squarely on a late night, 11:31 to 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before the essay was due, which is why she went straight to procedure after it; that night proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anything was on Owen's file right now, answer that plainly before laying out the October 15 outline, so the evidence lands on a parent who already feels her one non-negotiable is safe.
